channel.title: The MisterLibrarian Bible Project
channel.description: A fresh translation of the Bible into modern English, made from the original Hebrew and Greek one chapter at a time.

item.title: Romans 12
item.description: After the mercies of chapter 11, the letter turns to the practical half. “I urge you, then, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice” — a reasonable service, not a ritual, and an instruction not to be shaped by this age but transformed by…

item.title: Romans 11
item.description: “I say, then, God has not pushed away his people, has he? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” After the last verse of chapter 10 (“All day long I spread out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people”)…

item.title: Joshua 20
item.description: Jehovah speaks to Joshua for the last time in this book, in a sentence found nowhere else, and what he says is Numbers 35 with Moses’ name replaced: give for yourselves the cities of refuge. The man they protect is described with two phrases the older laws kept apart, BY…

item.title: Romans 7
item.description: “Or do you not know, brothers … that the law is lord over a man for as long as he lives?” Chapter 6 ended with the law standing at its edge (“you are not under law but under grace”), and chapter 7 takes it up with a picture from marriage law: a woman is bound to her husband…

item.title: Romans 10
item.description: “Brothers, the goodwill of my heart and my petition to God on their behalf are indeed for salvation.” After the stone of stumbling at the end of chapter 9, chapter 10 begins with a wish, a petition and a diagnosis: Israel has “a zeal for God, but not according to accurate…

item.title: Joshua 19
item.description: The other six lots come out in order. Simeon’s falls inside Judah’s own share, with thirteen cities counted and fourteen named, most of them towns Judah’s lists already hold. Zebulun’s border goes up ‘westward’ in a word that also means ‘to the sea,’ and passes Jonah’s town.…

item.title: Joshua 18
item.description: The congregation gathers at Shiloh and settles the tent of meeting, the land at last ‘subdued’ as Moses told Reuben and Gad it would have to be — and Joshua asks the seven tribes still without land how long they will go slack, the same root Pharaoh once turned on Israel.…

item.title: Romans 9
item.description: “I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying … I could pray to be, I myself, accursed, away from the Christ, on behalf of my brothers.” After the last verse of chapter 8 (“nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God”), chapter 9 opens…

item.title: Romans 6
item.description: “Shall we remain in sin, so that grace may increase?” The objection is built from the last verse of chapter 5, in the very verb of “where sin increased,” and Paul answers it with a fact before an order: “we who died to sin,” baptized “into his death,” “buried with him,”…

item.title: Romans 5
item.description: “Having been justified, then, out of faith, we have peace with God” — or “let us have,” since one vowel in the manuscripts turns the statement into an exhortation. ⚠ The first half is a chain: we boast in tribulation, because tribulation works out endurance, endurance proven…

item.title: Acts 28
item.description: Brought safely through, the party learns that the island is called Malta, and the barbarians show extraordinary kindness, kindling a fire; when Paul puts brushwood on it a viper fastens on his hand. ⚠ The islanders call him a murderer whom Justice has not allowed to live…

item.title: Acts 27
item.description: Paul and certain other prisoners are handed over to a centurion named Julius of the Augustan cohort, and ‘we’ set sail in a ship of Adramyttium with Aristarchus; at Sidon Julius treats Paul with kindness, and at Myra he puts the party on a ship of Alexandria bound for Italy.…

item.title: Acts 26
item.description: Agrippa tells Paul he may speak for himself, and Paul, stretching out his hand, says he counts himself happy to defend himself before a king who is an expert in the customs and questions of the Jews. ⚠ The road to Damascus is told a third time, with details the first two…

item.title: Acts 25
item.description: Festus, having entered the province, goes up after three days to Jerusalem, where the chief priests and the leading men give information against Paul and ask a favor against him — that he be sent for to Jerusalem, while they make an ambush to kill him on the way; Festus…

item.title: Acts 24
item.description: After five days the high priest Ananias comes down with some elders and an orator, Tertullus, who opens with praise for Felix’s ‘peace’ and ‘reforms’ and then calls Paul a plague, a stirrer-up of dissensions throughout the inhabited world and a ringleader of ‘the party of the…

item.title: Acts 23
item.description: Paul, staring at the Sanhedrin, says he has lived as a citizen before God in all good conscience — the verb whose noun, ‘citizenship,’ saved him from the lash the day before. The high priest Ananias has him struck on the mouth; Paul answers ‘God is going to strike you, you…

item.title: Acts 22
item.description: From the steps of the barracks Paul addresses the crowd in the Hebrew dialect, “Men, brothers and fathers,” and they give the more quiet: a Jewish man born in Tarsus, brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, a zealot of God who persecuted this Way to the death. ⚠ He…

item.title: Acts 21
item.description: Torn away from the Ephesian elders, Paul and his party make a straight run by Cos, Rhodes and Patara to Tyre, where disciples tell him “through the Spirit” not to set foot in Jerusalem, and on by Ptolemais to Caesarea and the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven…

item.title: Acts 20
item.description: After the uproar ceases Paul sends for the disciples, greets them and goes on into Macedonia and Greece, where a plot by the Jews on the eve of his sailing for Syria turns him back through Macedonia, with seven companions named; the narration returns to “we” at Philippi and…

item.title: Acts 19
item.description: Paul comes to Ephesus while Apollos is at Corinth and asks twelve disciples, “Did you receive Holy Spirit when you believed?” — they have not even heard whether there is one, and know only John’s baptism; they are baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, Paul lays hands on…

item.title: Acts 18
item.description: Paul goes from Athens to Corinth and finds Aquila and Priscilla, Jews lately come from Italy because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to depart from Rome, and works with them as a tentmaker; when Silas and Timothy come down from Macedonia he is “gripped by the word,” and…

item.title: Acts 17
item.description: Paul and Silas pass through Amphipolis and Apollonia to Thessalonica, where for three sabbaths Paul “opens up” the Scriptures to show that the Christ had to suffer and rise, and a mob made up of marketplace men goes looking for them at Jason’s house, drags Jason before the…

item.title: Acts 16
item.description: Paul takes Timothy — a Jewish mother, a Greek father, “well spoken of” — and circumcises him “because of the Jews,” and the cities are handed “the decrees that had been decided” at Jerusalem. ⚠ The Holy Spirit hinders them from speaking the word in Asia and the Spirit of…

item.title: Acts 13
item.description: At Antioch the prophets and teachers — Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen who was brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul — are ministering and fasting when the Holy Spirit says, “Set apart, then, for me Barnabas and Saul.” ⚠ Sent out, they sail…

item.title: Acts 12
item.description: Herod the king lays his hands on some of the congregation, kills James the brother of John “with a sword” and, seeing that it pleases the Jews, arrests Peter in the days of the Unleavened Bread — four groups of four soldiers, a bringing-out planned for “after the Passover.” ⚠…

item.title: Acts 14
item.description: At Iconium the pair go into the synagogue again and a great number of Jews and Greeks believe; the Jews who disobeyed stir up and afflict the souls of the nations, the city is split between the Jews and “the apostles,” and when an impulse comes to treat them outrageously and…

item.title: Acts 11
item.description: Peter goes up to Jerusalem and is called to account by “those of the circumcision” for going in to uncircumcised men and eating with them — a meal chapter 10 never narrates — and tells the story again “in orderly sequence,” with the housetop and the hunger gone, “wild beasts”…

item.title: Acts 10
item.description: At Caesarea a centurion named Cornelius, “devout and fearing God,” whose prayers and alms “went up as a memorial before God,” is told by an angel to send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter; the KJV and Geneva add words at vv6 and 32 and “fasting” at v30 that the printed…

item.title: Acts 9
item.description: Saul, still “breathing threat and murder,” asks the high priest for letters to the synagogues of Damascus, and a light, a doubled name and “Why are you persecuting me?” stop him on the road; the words the KJV adds at vv5–6 are not in the printed Greek, and the companions’…

item.title: Acts 8
item.description: The persecution that scatters the congregation out of Jerusalem: Saul, who was “approving” Stephen’s killing in the last verse of chapter 7, now “ravages” the congregation house by house, and the scattered go through the land bringing good news with one verb while Philip, one…
